episode_title: Building the next chapter with Jordan Schupan

real_qa.q: How did Schupan Sons grow from a five-person scrapyard in Kalamazoo, Michigan to 600 employees across 18 locations?
real_qa.r: Schupan Sons was started by Jordan's grandfather as a five-person scrapyard in Kalamazoo, Michigan, primarily to support his family after his death. Under his father Mark's 53-year leadership, the company grew by listening to the market and customers. They expanded from industrial accounts into the beverage deposit space, aluminum EBC processing and trading, metal service centers selling new materials, and precision machining and fabrication work across multiple states. The company now operates 18 locations with 600 employees.
real_qa.requete: Schupan Sons growth history employees locations

real_qa.q: What was Jordan Schupan's career path before joining Schupan Sons as CEO in 2017?
real_qa.r: Jordan worked in software startups at the Series A and B stage, where one company went public and another was acquired. He started in sales roles in fast-paced, venture-backed growth environments where job security depended quarter-to-quarter on sales numbers. In 2016, after earning money from selling enterprise software licenses, he traveled around the world for a few months. He was also close to joining Snowflake at the time, but decided to pursue opportunities in the family business instead.
real_qa.requete: Jordan Schupan career before Schupan Sons CEO

real_qa.q: What role did Tom Emerick play in bringing Jordan Schupan back to the family business?
real_qa.r: Tom Emerick, the COO who has been with Schupan Sons for 35 years and helped build the foundation of the beverage business, came out to California to recruit Jordan back to the company. Emerick presented a trading business opportunity that was at the time just on a sheet of paper and told him this would be a good time to rejoin the family business. He has been instrumental in working with Jordan through the leadership transition.
real_qa.requete: Tom Emerick Schupan Sons COO 35 years

real_qa.q: How did Schupan Sons expand from a Midwest processor to a national aluminum trader?
real_qa.r: When Jordan joined in January 2017, Schupan Sons was primarily a Midwest processor. He worked with Andy McKee, who became a great partner in building out the trading business. Together they had opportunities to buy metal from more places beyond the Midwest, expanding the company's reach nationally. Jordan handled West Coast buying operations and spent considerable time in Michigan, while Andy expanded sourcing from additional regions, transforming the company from regional to national scope.
real_qa.requete: Schupan Sons national aluminum trading expansion

real_qa.q: What motivated Jordan Schupan to leave the software startup world and return to Schupan Sons?
real_qa.r: After gaining independence and financial success in 2016, Jordan reflected on what truly motivated him long-term. He realized the family business had been around almost 50 years with an incredible brand, and it was how he and his father had always connected since childhood. He worried that if something happened and he had not taken the opportunity to work with his father, he would regret it. He also recognized the potential impact of being part of a private company with only a few owners, where business success directly benefits employees, and the stability of long-term shareholders with great people.
real_qa.requete: Jordan Schupan why return family business Schupan Sons

guest.bio_context: Jordan Schupan is the third-generation leader of Schupan Sons, a family-owned scrap metal business founded by his grandfather nearly 60 years ago in Kalamazoo, Michigan. Before returning to the family business in January 2017, he worked in software startups in the enterprise space at Series A and B stages (where one went public and one was acquired), traded equity options in Chicago, and spent time in sales roles in fast-paced growth environments. His father Mark led the company for 53 years before transitioning to chairman when Jordan became CEO.
